view.lede: The Hill Track, left-handed: one of the five generic courses that every course without its own build races on for now (stiff, uphill finish). A pear-shaped course of about 1m5f, wide at the stands end and narrow at the far end: a tight downhill turn into a 4f run-in that climbs all the way to the post, and a stiff 6f sprint course uphill from start to finish. Dressed as a hilltop course.
notes: Beverley, Carlisle, Hamilton, Pontefract, Bath, Chepstow (undulating).
About 13.6f round, a 4.03f run-in. Drawn from a few numbers (the corners and bends of the loop, the chutes), so it can be reshaped quickly.
Hilltop course: medium and smaller pieces from the grandstand crib sheet on one front line, the crowd up to the rail; the festival in the infield opposite and up the stand side.
Choose Medium or Low under Quality in the race view's bar. Auto steps down by itself.
